attributes.summary: Attached this repo to agent-plan-visualiser tracking: confirmed exfu-agent-plan-visualiser@exfu already enabled globally, ran apv-init to create .apv/ (events.jsonl, schema-version.txt, bin/apv), .apv-config.toml, ./apv symlink, .gitignore for local-only state, and installed pre-commit/pre-push/reference-transaction git hooks. Operator approved adding the CLAUDE.md orientation block; re-ran apv-init --accept-claude-md to append it.

Top-level intent for ExFu Humane Agents: conventions for the human-agent interface — agents designed around human limits (attention, working memory, context), shipped as standalone skills in one plugin. Themes: Communication, Interaction, Mechanisms. Authored draft; acceptance ceremony pending.

Communication theme: what agents emit for humans. Principles: dual-audience separation, outcome-first, hard budgets, jargon zero-tolerance, caveats survive translation. Units: U1 exfu-reporting (shipped v0), U2 progress narration, U3 notifications.
M1: the plugin exists and ships its first convention. DoD: repo scaffolded (done), exfu-reporting shipped with evidence (done), marketplace installability (pending, external), README thesis (done).

Retrospective executable-cold brief for the exfu-reporting skill (dual-audience reporting: Agent Report + Human Report). Implementation already done 2026-08-18 and transplanted from agent-planning-and-delegating branch claude/dual-format-reporting-skill-dae67d; RED/GREEN verification recorded in the brief. Completion events await plan acceptance (draft gate).

decisions.text: Operator rulings (chat, 2026-08-18): (1) the reporting skill is a 'humane agents' concern — the human-agent interface — not a planning-stack utility; it gets its own project and proper plugin (exfu-humane-agents) rather than living in exfu-agent-planning-and-delegating or a utils drawer; (2) repo created and apv-inited by the operator, contents bootstrapped this session with the skill transplanted from the planner repo branch; (3) all four plans authored draft — acceptance is the operator's ceremony and has not been performed, so no implementation events are recorded against them yet despite the skill file landing in this commit (the T3 creation summary carries that state honestly).
